newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa jumps after Ivorian minister's remarks.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa jumps after Ivorian minister's remarks.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa jumped as producers got the upper hand after bullish remarks by an Ivorian minister, traders said.
"The producers have got the buyers on the run," one said.
Reports of Ivorian commodities minister Alain Gauze's ideas on production, along with plans to do away with illegal output from national forests helped the market up, he said.
Short covering took the May contract through resistance at 972 stg, while origin sellers were confining themselves to selling "bits and pieces."
May last traded 35 stg up at 981 stg. May volume was 7,200 lots of a total 12,541.
The Ivory Coast's 1996/97 cocoa crop will be below one million tonnes and it has already sold around 800,000 tonnes, Gauze said.
It has no more to sell, he said to journalists at an International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) meeting in London.
Gauze said that the government had decided to destroy all coffee and cocoa planted illegally in national forests.
Speaking to reporters at the International Cocoa Organization talks Gauze said that these illegal plantings had amounted to around 100,000 tonnes of cocoa and coffee last year.
